To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a novel algorithm for optimal user scheduling and resource allocation in 802. 11ax which is optimal under the assumption of multiple RUs per user and that we have developed two practical algorithms which jointly split the bandwidth into R Us and schedule users/user groups on them.
the optimal scheduling algorithm for 802.11ac can be used for 802.1ax with a minor modification.

the optimal scheduling and resource allocation algorithm is a divide and conquer algorithm that is based on a novel greedy heuristic and that two practical algorithms achieve near-optimal performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of scheduling users and user groups over subcarriers in the context of the new 802.11 ax WiFi standard.
the design of scheduling and resource allocation schemes for 802.11ac and we make the following contributions.
the problem of how to optimally schedule users and user groups in a frequency selective environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed algorithms are optimal and practical for 802.11 ax scheduling.

the optimal solution is a greedy algorithm that assigns the user groups to the subcarriers with best channel gain and then allocates the users within the groups to the subcarrier with the highest channel gain.
our practical algorithms are able to achieve very good performance and that the divide and conquer algorithm is optimal under the assumption of multiple RUs per user.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the optimal solution for the problem at hand can be found by a divide and conquer approach.
our practical algorithms are able to achieve near-optimal performance in terms of user sum rate in 802.1ax OFDMA systems.
our proposed algorithms can achieve a sum rate very close to the optimal sum rate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 802.1ax scheduling problem can be solved efficiently with low complexity algorithms.
the 802.1ax standard should allow users/user groups to be assigned to more RUs than one to achieve optimal performance.
the optimal solution for the actual problem is very close to the tight upper bound and hence, the optimal scheduling algorithm can be used in practice.
